# Milesight WS202 PIR & Light Sensor - Implementation Documentation

## Overview
Complete Berry driver implementation for Milesight WS202 PIR & Light Sensor with LoRaWAN connectivity.

**Generation Date**: 2025-01-09  
**Driver Version**: v1.0  
**Vendor**: Milesight  
**Model**: WS202  
**Source Document**: [WS202 User Guide](https://resource.milesight.com/milesight/iot/document/ws202-user-guide-en.pdf)

### Key Features
- Complete PIR motion detection with occupied/vacant states
- Light level detection with bright/dark states
- Battery monitoring (percentage)
- Device information reporting (SN, versions, class)
- Power-on event detection
- Optimized for ESP32 memory constraints

### Display Format
The driver uses emoji-only display for web UI:
- 🚫 Motion detected / 🆓 No motion
- 🌞 Bright (light detected) / 🌕 Dark (no light)
- ℹ️ Device information
- Battery indicator with percentage

## Integration Examples

### Basic Configuration
```berry
# Load the decoder in Tasmota
load("WS202.be")

# Configure via LoRaWAN settings
# LoRaWanDecoder1 WS202.be
# LoRaWanName1 Office-PIR
```

### Testing Payload Decoding
```berry
# Test with sample payloads from the documentation

# Example 1: Basic sensor data - Battery 100%, PIR Occupied, Light Bright
# Payload: 01 75 64 03 00 01 04 00 01
var test_payload = bytes("01756403000104000")
var decoded = LwDeco.decodeUplink("TestWS202", 1, -80, 85, test_payload)
print(decoded)
# Expected: {'battery': 100, 'pir_status': 'occupied', 'motion_detected': true, 'light_status': 'bright', 'light_detected': true}

# Example 2: Device information on power-on
# Payload: ff0bff ff0101 ff086538b2232131 ff090100 ff0a0101 ff0f00
var power_on_payload = bytes("ff0bffff0101ff086538b2232131ff090100ff0a0101ff0f00")
var decoded2 = LwDeco.decodeUplink("TestWS202", 1, -80, 85, power_on_payload)
print(decoded2)
# Expected: {'power_on': true, 'protocol_version': 1, 'device_sn': '6538B2232131', 'hardware_version': 'V1.0', 'software_version': 'V1.1', 'device_class': 'Class A'}

# Example 3: PIR vacant, Light dark, Battery 75%
var test_payload3 = bytes("01754B03000004000")
var decoded3 = LwDeco.decodeUplink("TestWS202", 1, -80, 85, test_payload3)
print(decoded3)
# Expected: {'battery': 75, 'pir_status': 'vacant', 'motion_detected': false, 'light_status': 'dark', 'light_detected': false}
```

### Downlink Commands (Reference)
The WS202 supports the following downlink commands (not implemented in decoder):
- Set Reporting Interval: `ff03` + 2 bytes (seconds, little-endian)
- Reboot Device: `ff10ff`

Example downlink to set 20-minute interval:
```
ff03b004  # 0x04b0 = 1200 seconds = 20 minutes
```

## Technical Details

### Data Format
- All multi-byte values use little-endian encoding
- Channel format: `[Channel ID][Type][Data...]`
- Supports chained channel data in single uplink

### PIR Status Values
- `0x00`: Vacant (no motion detected)
- `0x01`: Occupied (motion detected)

### Light Status Values
- `0x00`: Dark (no light detected)
- `0x01`: Bright (light detected)

### Battery Reporting
- Reported as percentage (0-100)
- Low battery alert triggered at <10%
- Device sends single uplink when battery drops below threshold

## Notes
- The WS202 has configurable idle time for PIR vacant reporting (default 120s)
- Light threshold for bright/dark states is configurable via NFC
- Device supports Milesight D2D protocol for direct device communication
- Supports both Standard-Channel and Single-Channel modes for LoRaWAN
